newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour leftist Livingstone wants big tax rises.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour leftist Livingstone wants big tax rises.

text.p: Ken Livingstone, a leading left-wing backbench member of parliament in Britain's Labour party, on Friday called for substantial tax rises and said he did not think there would be any privatisations under the new government.
"I don't think there will be any privatisations," he said in an interview with BBC radio after Labour's landslide election victory.

He said Labour would inherit public finances in much worse state than the Conservatives had acknowledged and the way to tackle this was through "substantial tax increases, mainly on the corporate sector."

Livingstone was former leader of the now disbanded Greater London Council and is a leading representative of traditional socialist "Old Labour" from which party leader Tony Blair has distanced himself.
Livingstone said he did not want taxes to rise for ordinary middle-income families, who already faced a painful tax burden.

"In a sense Britain is an under-taxed society. Our government takes less tax than any other except Portugal in the European Union," he said. "It's the tax on the corporate sector in Britain which has become almost voluntary."
He rejected suggestions that there would be "civil war" between Labour leftists and Blair's centrist leadership.

"I don't think there will. There will be sharp debates and major arguments about priorities, but we aren't going to get the Labour party tearing itself apart because there's an incredible enthusiasm. This has electrified us and changed politics."
